source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use a hierarchy of administrative measures, environmental controls, and respiratory protective equipment for healthcare TB infection control.","B":"Use contact precautions, surgical hand antisepsis, and environmental surface disinfection as the three levels of TB control.","C":"Use staff antibiotic prophylaxis, ultraviolet exposure, and elimination of symptom screening as the three control levels.","D":"Use standard precautions alone, because a separate respiratory-protection component is not part of healthcare TB control."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC describes a three-level hierarchy for healthcare TB infection control: administrative measures, environmental controls, and respiratory protective equipment. Administrative measures are the first and most important level and include prompt recognition and management of people with suspected infectious TB.
